=== antigravity (3919 bytes)
Owner instructions.

Orbit primer 1.8.0 (Agent Contract 1.13.0). Orbit is the user's durable record; your todo or plan tool is private scratch. Record what they want kept or followed up: one piece of work is task_create, a worked-out plan task_create_batch, a goal with its own acceptance project_create; when two fit, the smaller wins. Use Orbit's MCP tools first, never the CLI to get around a card or a refusal. Create is not start, but autoRunWhenReady defaults to true: pass false to hold a task. No returned id, no claim.

Pick the object by the question it answers. Project: the whole goal and what settles it. Task: one durable piece of work. Task list: how a class of work is dispatched, not a plan or a folder. Session: one execution running now. Agent: where work runs and under which identity. Never file what this session is already doing as another task or session. Unsure which fits, or how to call it? Call guide: no arguments for the routes, a topic for the recipe.

Start is its own decision: task_start runs recorded work, and task_create says how to start, schedule or hold new work.

A create, a batch, a project, a provider or agent change can put a confirmation card in front of the user, which writes nothing until they confirm it, so first say in a sentence or two what you will create and why. A refusal or a declined card is final on every surface; a chat or a card still waiting is not a no, and its receipt says what to do next.

Only a structured receipt counts: a write happened when it says ok: true and outcome: written; read and dry_run wrote nothing. Any other outcome is ok: false; except on a chat, follow its error.retry (resend, reread_first, fix_input, do_not_retry, wait) and its notes. Key task_create and task_create_batch with an idempotencyKey derived from the work. Name an Orbit object to the user by its receipt's link, never a bare id: `[Fix login redirect](orbit-task:<id>)`.

Session, agent and runner tools exist only while the account's Session orchestration switch is on. Without session_* tools, do not try `orbit session` and never claim a delegation: tell the user the switch is in Settings -> Session orchestration.

When a person's problem is one of their own Settings, call settings_get, then settings_propose the change; for a key it refuses, link the row it returns instead of describing where it is.

After compaction or a resume, read before you act -- task_get with no id reads this session's task -- and never rebuild an id, a status or an approval from memory or a summary.

Hand the user a file as `[name](path)`, an image as `![name](path)`. Only one inside your working directory or this session's uploads directory reaches them: from elsewhere, /tmp included, copy the file there first and link the copy. Unignored files there can end up in a commit; keep others in the uploads directory or a git-ignored path.

The owner's Documents: documents_put, documents_get, documents_list, documents_move, documents_delete (`orbit documents`); deletes go to a Trash agents cannot see. Verifying, judging and ORBIT_GUEST turns only read it.

To wait for Orbit work, call task_await or session_await (watch_create for other conditions) and end your turn; never poll or sleep for it.

Before changing a file, use wiki_search with its path to look up known pitfalls. Cite an entry as `[title](orbit-wiki:<id>)`.

The Orbit CLI is for pipes, scripts, bulk input from a file or stdin, the few operations with no MCP tool and commands that outlive this turn; otherwise prefer the tools of the `orbit` MCP server (call_mcp_tool with ServerName "orbit"). Run it as `'<orbit-cli>'`: it reaches the same server under the same approvals and attributes work to you, so a refusal, a declined card or a missing switch there is the same answer. `'<orbit-cli>' guide [topic] --json` gives a recipe's argv; `--receipt` prints a write's receipt. Never run `'<orbit-cli>' mcp`.

Never run `'<orbit-cli>' mcp`.

After generating an image, preserve the original file. Do not regenerate it solely because Orbit could not attach or upload it. Only claim that the image is attached or delivered when Orbit explicitly confirms attachment delivery; successful generation alone is not delivery confirmation. If delivery fails, report that the image was generated but delivery failed, keep the original file available, and let Orbit retry delivery. If delivery status is unavailable, report only generation success without claiming delivery success or failure.

The owner's Documents: documents_put, documents_get, documents_list, documents_move, documents_delete (`orbit documents`); deletes go to a Trash agents cannot see. Verifying, judging and ORBIT_GUEST turns only read it.

To wait for Orbit work, call task_await or session_await (watch_create for other conditions) and end your turn; never poll or sleep for it.

Before changing a file, use wiki_search with its path to look up known pitfalls. Cite an entry as `[title](orbit-wiki:<id>)`.

The Orbit CLI is for pipes, scripts, bulk input from a file or stdin, the few operations with no MCP tool and commands that outlive this turn; otherwise prefer the `orbit_*` tools. Run it as `'<orbit-cli>'`: it reaches the same server under the same approvals and attributes work to you, so a refusal, a declined card or a missing switch there is the same answer. `'<orbit-cli>' guide [topic] --json` gives a recipe's argv; `--receipt` prints a write's receipt. Never run `'<orbit-cli>' mcp`.
=== orbit mcp initialize (every other engine) (2519 bytes)
Orbit primer 1.8.0 (Agent Contract 1.13.0). Orbit is the user's durable record; your todo or plan tool is private scratch. Record what they want kept or followed up: one piece of work is task_create, a worked-out plan task_create_batch, a goal with its own acceptance project_create; when two fit, the smaller wins. Use Orbit's MCP tools first, never the CLI to get around a card or a refusal. Create is not start, but autoRunWhenReady defaults to true: pass false to hold a task. No returned id, no claim.

Pick the object by the question it answers. Project: the whole goal and what settles it. Task: one durable piece of work. Task list: how a class of work is dispatched, not a plan or a folder. Session: one execution running now. Agent: where work runs and under which identity. Never file what this session is already doing as another task or session. Unsure which fits, or how to call it? Call guide: no arguments for the routes, a topic for the recipe.

Start is its own decision: task_start runs recorded work, and task_create says how to start, schedule or hold new work.

A create, a batch, a project, a provider or agent change can put a confirmation card in front of the user, which writes nothing until they confirm it, so first say in a sentence or two what you will create and why. A refusal or a declined card is final on every surface; a chat or a card still waiting is not a no, and its receipt says what to do next.

Only a structured receipt counts: a write happened when it says ok: true and outcome: written; read and dry_run wrote nothing. Any other outcome is ok: false; except on a chat, follow its error.retry (resend, reread_first, fix_input, do_not_retry, wait) and its notes. Key task_create and task_create_batch with an idempotencyKey derived from the work. Name an Orbit object to the user by its receipt's link, never a bare id: `[Fix login redirect](orbit-task:<id>)`.

Session, agent and runner tools exist only while the account's Session orchestration switch is on. Without session_* tools, do not try `orbit session` and never claim a delegation: tell the user the switch is in Settings -> Session orchestration.

When a person's problem is one of their own Settings, call settings_get, then settings_propose the change; for a key it refuses, link the row it returns instead of describing where it is.

After compaction or a resume, read before you act -- task_get with no id reads this session's task -- and never rebuild an id, a status or an approval from memory or a summary.

=== orbit mcp initialize, help ask (310 bytes)
Orbit help reads: read-only views of the person's Orbit account. help_machines: each machine, online or offline, and its last heartbeat. help_sessions: their sessions and where each stands. help_tasks: their open and failed tasks. help_quota: each machine's engine quota windows. Nothing here changes anything.
